### BLOCKER — independently confirmed by the orchestrator before acting

Plan v1 §4.2(A) step 2 built the permanent-home set from **unscoped** whole-repo
basenames (`git` tree listing for `origin/issue-<N>` **and** `HEAD`). Replaying
v1's own §6 item 2 FAIL-direction test against the live tree (178,914 tracked

|---|---|---|
| `pilot_gate_report.json` | **8** | `eval_results/issue_{1417 x2, 1739 x3, 1774, 2094 x2}/` |
| `upload_done.json` | **4** | `eval_results/issue_1768/{model_text_2x2, on_target, on_target_r4, on_target_r5}/` |
| `stage2_results.json` | 0 | — |

So for a no-permanent-home issue, residue = {`stage2_results.json`} only:
**2 of the 3 motivating losses false-PASS today.** Both colliding names are
CONVENTIONAL — `pilot_gate_report.json` is the built-in #2054 pilot-gate output
name, `upload_done.json` a recurring completion-marker name — so incident
classes 1 and 3 would have been structurally invisible to the new check BY
DESIGN, permanently. v1's §6 item 2 acceptance criterion ("FAIL naming all
three files") was false as written, and §8's "basename collision — Low
likelihood" was wrong by an order of magnitude for the whole-tree form.

Root cause of the miss: v1's §12 assumption-1 predicate trace covered only the
pre-recovery INCIDENT-TIME tree, never the tree the check actually runs against.
This is the exact failure mode #2187 exists to prevent, reproduced one level up
in the fix's own verification design — caught pre-implementation, which is the
point of the floor.

(issue token as a path component) BEFORE taking basenames. Verified to preserve
the PASS direction — all four recovered #2162 files sit under
`eval_results/issue_2162/` on `origin/issue-2162`. The HF arm is unchanged
(caller-supplied prefixes are issue-scoped by construction). The regression pin
is the assertion that FAIL names ALL THREE basenames against the live repo: it
fails under v1's design and passes under the scoped one.
